scope: Independent read-only design/draft review of four-cylinder even-fire sequential fuel/spark using unchanged MissingTooth crank decoding plus one rising cam edge per720 degrees. No production edits, child agents, target execution or physical qualification.
result: The current portable design is a sound minimal direction after the pending-cam and inactive-phase-watchdog fixes. Target integration remains in progress and requires the explicit contracts below. This is not final implementation or physical-engine approval.
verified_draft_improvements: Wrapper-owned phase_tooth0..2*slots carries720 parity into AngleScheduler; scheduler.cut reset therefore cannot silently select the opposite revolution.
Crank history retains64 decoded timestamp/angle samples. Pending cam retry preserves immediate crank scheduling instead of delaying the entire trigger stream by1ms.
One pending cam is sufficient for the specified1ms reorder interval: a second real cam cannot arrive that soon at the supported RPM, so another pulse is a duplicate/error.
Both acquisition pulses must be consecutive cycle matches (shift+2), so a360-degree extra pulse cannot be ignored while accepting the next720 pulse.
PhaseDecoder faults remain sticky until reset. Cam window, cycle, order, mapping, timeout and crank-loss reasons are separately observable.
Executor now retains cam alarm/expiry while inactive, checks old expiry before accepting deadline extensions and preserves CamPhase fault after attempted renewal.
Sequential controller mass divides by one opening per720, adds dead time once, and computes injector duty on the720 interval. Batch retains two openings and per-opening dead time.
Sequential injection is scheduled by its end-angle target before start; an already high injector retains its low edge. Full dwell and latched spark advance follow existing semantics.

independent_native_probe.method: Fresh -std=c++17 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -fsanitize=address,undefined build against a copied draft header snapshot.
independent_native_probe.interpretation: At120slots/8000RPM, delaying every crank callback by1000us while cam is timely acquires phase. Introducing that skew after lock retains phase. Inactive sequential phase arms3001us and dispatch/renewal at3001/3002 latches cam_phase_lost. These confirm fixes that landed before the independent probe snapshot.

required_target_contracts: Keep the legacy MissingTooth decoder implementation and group0 rising-edge capture contract. PhaseDecoder owns crank revolution/history/parity in task context; no floating-point phase mapping enters the capture ISR.

Publish crank_synced separately from phase_synced/phase state. Sequential outputs stay globally low while acquiring. Absence of phase before first acquisition must not create a bootstrap fault that prevents acquisition.
Validate cam ingress age with fresh GPTimer now, as for crank. Distinguish ingress delay from bounded pending-mapping delay. Do not use a captured timestamp as a proxy for current processing time.

Process every current-epoch crank/cam for phase/history even when a capture is too old relative to the latest control command to schedule from it. Command/sample freshness does not invalidate mechanical phase observations by itself.

Never build a scheduling candidate using cam capture time paired with the latest crank phase_tooth. Wait for the next eligible crank or use an explicitly stored matching crank timestamp/position sample.

The executor must enforce phase expiry before a fresh phase update, command update or candidate commit. PhaseDecoder.cam and pending acceptance should either receive/check fresh processing time or have an explicit caller precondition preventing wrapper deadline renewal before expiry is checked.

A cam phase guard remains armed after acquisition through selective fuel/spark cuts and inactive/OverRev control states. A missing/duplicate/out-of-window/unmappable/late cam after acquisition cuts and latches; never automatically switch to batch or reacquire while moving.

Commit generation/epoch validation covers phase acquisition/loss, guard changes, global cuts, ISR expiry, controller command sequence and configuration changes. A stale candidate must not restore a cleared phase flag or extend an expired deadline.

Publish phase validity with its accepted configuration/phase epoch. A cached old phase_synced=true must not make the first new-revision active command trip a permanent CamPhase fault before new phase can be acquired.

Use existing configuration hold around persistence/publication. Changes to strategy, wheel, tooth reference, firing order, cam center/window or injection reference invalidate phase/history/pending records and scheduler generations. A configuration edit must not clear a latched timing/phase fault while moving.

Stopped recovery requires raw quiet on both crank and cam, fresh valid stopped samples, acknowledged global-low outputs and continuous20ms supervision. Cam-only activity must prevent recovery. After recovery, clear history/pending/parity and require two fresh cam pulses again.
Keep selected N16R8 physical output writes compiled out. Strategy configuration changes logical scheduling only.

angle_and_event_contract.cylinder_identity: GPIO injector1..4 and coil1..4 remain cylinder identities. For a cylinder1-first firing order, cylinder compression phases are180*position_in_order. A general permutation can be cyclically rotated around cylinder1; current draft instead explicitly validates cylinder1 first.
angle_and_event_contract.reference: With tooth zero at configured tooth1_btdc_deg before cylinder1 TDC, spark goal is tooth1_btdc_deg+cylinder_phase-latched_advance modulo720. Injector end goal is tooth1_btdc_deg+cylinder_phase+injection_end_deg modulo720.
angle_and_event_contract.fuel_mass: Sequential width is full-cycle fuel mass/flow + one dead time; it is not twice the complete batch width. One injector opening and one coil firing occur per cylinder per720 after startup skips.
angle_and_event_contract.injection_end: End angle is a pre-start target. After start, fixed pulse duration/closing deadline preserves fuel mass; actual end angle may move under acceleration. Late unreachable starts retain a committed full pulse or skip one complete720 cycle, never issue a partial injection.
angle_and_event_contract.advance: Advance is latched at dwell start. Subsequent tooth correction can move the off time for that latched angle only within maximum physical high-time guards.

deadline_policy_assessment: The next expected cam center must be a fixed angular-cycle identity, not recomputed from each arriving command or from an arbitrary latest cam. Per-tooth speed updates may reproject the same center/window close; expiry must be checked before extending.

A1ms allowance accounts for software timing, not uncertain future shaft acceleration. An absolute wall-clock deadline cannot be guaranteed to equal angular closure under arbitrary changing RPM while the worker has no fresh angle information.

Bounded extrapolation near a missing-tooth gap can reject a physically valid cam during speed ripple. Either quantify a supported acceleration/phase-uncertainty envelope or explicitly accept conservative phase inhibition. The draft comment accepts this limitation; it should remain visible in evidence and UI qualification.
Independent producer/tooth/high-time watchdogs remain essential. They protect output shutdown when phase-worker progress stops, alongside the separately armed cam deadline.

Define boundary semantics for a cam at the latest allowed window angle with maximum processing delay. Timer expiry and validation racing at exactly the same microsecond must have an explicit fail-closed ordering and adequate quantization/clock uncertainty padding.
minimum_next_tests: Both starting revolution parities, all supported cam centers including0/360/720 wrap and missing gaps, multiple wheel geometries and all six cylinder1-first firing orders.
Cam callback late, crank callbacks late, alternating skew, ties and reversed callback order through the1ms bound; history eviction and pending-overflow/error cases.

Independently angle-generated acceleration, deceleration and compression-speed ripple, with cam angle fixed mechanically. Include narrow windows in long missing-tooth gaps and qualify conservative false faults.
Missing cam, extra360-degree cam, same-timestamp and near-window duplicates, out-of-order/late/unmappable cam, crank sync loss after acquisition and no moving fallback/reacquisition.
Cam timeout during inactive control, selective cuts and OverRev; old deadline versus cam refresh/command refresh/candidate commit races; stale phase epoch across tune/trigger changes.
Raw cam activity while crank is quiet prevents stopped recovery. Old queued cam records cannot seed acquisition after configuration/recovery.

Full-cycle delivered fuel mass and per-opening dead-time accounting; injector end target versus fixed closing time under RPM changes; spark once720 with latched advance/full dwell; first-cycle skip behavior.
Legacy batch regressions and old tune imports remain valid; invalid strategy/order/angles rejected; selected physical outputs stay inhibited.

After target integration, rebuild selected/dummy images and audit complete ISR code/literal/data closure, including new integer guard fields. No native test substitutes for hardware capture/output timing measurements.
qualification_limits: Two repeatable cam pulses establish parity relative to the configured reference, not the correctness of the physical cylinder1 compression calibration. A360-degree calibration error is undetectable from this single cam pattern alone.
Existing MCPWM capture overwrite, separate timestamp/polarity register behavior, physical input conditioning and timer/IRQ latency remain unmeasured.
This review makes no engine, electrical or vehicle qualification claim. No hardware was connected or flashed.
